title: Fix the page's UnsafeStack

blocks.text: The page's Q6 walks through a broken `UnsafeStack`: `elements` and `size` are shared mutable state, `pop()` is a **check-then-act** and `size++` / `--size` are **read-modify-write** actions. Its checklist says every read **and** write must be protected by the same lock; guarding the writes alone still leaves a data race.
Write `SafeStack<T>`, a stack of up to any number of items, backed by an array that starts with 16 slots and doubles when full:

items: `push(T item)` adds an item on top;
`pop()` removes and returns the top item, or throws `java.util.EmptyStackException` when the stack is empty (the size stays `0`);
`size()` returns how many items it holds.

blocks.text: Every method, reads included, holds the stack's own monitor (`this`), so a caller can also hold `synchronized (stack)` around a compound action of its own.

cases.says: pop() returns the items in the reverse of the order they were pushed, and size() follows.
pop() on an empty stack checks first and throws EmptyStackException, leaving the size at zero.
The stack grows past its first sixteen slots instead of failing.
Reads take the same lock as writes, so size() waits while another thread holds the stack's monitor.

concepts: Check-then-act and read-modify-write steps must run under one lock.
A synchronized wrapper needs the caller to hold its lock for iteration and compound actions.
Reads must take the same lock as writes; synchronizing only the writes still leaves a data race.
